comments.body:
## Mathematical Review (critic-agent)

**Verdict.** The answer is CORRECT: for every fixed i, lim_n σ_i(H_n)=π. The core argument
(Theorem 1) — monotone increase via Cauchy interlacing, upper bound + strictness via empty point
spectrum, lower bound via an i-dim subspace of the top spectral subspace + min–max — is essentially
correct and complete. I verified the constant bookkeeping in Lemma 4 symbolically
(2(i+1)δ=ε/(20π), 10π(i+1)δ=ε/4) and the conclusion numerically (σ_i(H_n)↑π for i=1,2,3; slow
1/log n rate). Two items fall short of the cite-precisely / prove-fully standard and are filed as
gaps below.

### Background / tools
- Hilbert's inequality (HLP Thm 315): Σ a_i a_j/(i+j−1) ≤ π Σ a_i², π sharp ⇒ 0≤H≤πI, ‖H‖=π.
  Positivity also from 1/(i+j−1)=∫₀¹ t^{i+j−2}dt ⇒ ⟨Hx,x⟩=∫₀¹|Σx_k t^{k−1}|²dt.
- Spectrum (Magnus 1950, Rosenblum 1958, Power Ch.3): H ≅ M_φ, φ(t)=π/cosh(πt), so σ(H)=[0,π],
  purely continuous (no eigenvalues).
- Cauchy interlacing (Horn–Johnson Thm 4.3.17) ⇒ σ_i(H_n) nondecreasing in n (H_n is leading
  principal submatrix of H_{n+1}).
- Courant–Fischer min–max (Horn–Johnson Thm 4.2.6).
- de Bruijn–Wilf (1962): π−σ_1(H_n) ∼ π³/ln n (leading order; large ln ln n correction).

### Proof structure required
(1) 0≤H≤πI, ‖H‖=π [Lemma 1 ✓]. (2) E((π−ε,π]) nonzero of infinite rank [Lemma 2 — see Gap A].
(3) σ_i(H_n)<π via π∉σ_p(H) [Lemma 3 ✓]. (4) monotonicity via interlacing [Lemma 3 ✓].
(5) lower bound via truncating an i-dim U⊂ran E to V_N + min–max [Lemma 4 ✓, constants correct].
(6) combine ⇒ limit = π [Theorem 1 ✓].

### Gap A (moderate) — Lemma 2 spectral input only cited, not established
The lower bound needs rank E((π−ε,π])=∞ for all ε>0. Lemma 1 gives only ‖H‖=π ⇒ π∈σ(H) ⇒
E((π−ε,π])≠0, NOT infinite-rank. Infinite rank genuinely requires the continuous-spectrum fact,
which is only sketched (Mellin equivalence to M_{π/cosh πt}). Need: precise statement+hypothesis
check of Magnus's theorem, OR a self-contained soft proof exhibiting, for every ε>0 and m, an
m-dim S_m with ⟨Hx,x⟩≥(π−ε)‖x‖² (disjointly-supported far-shifted near-extremizers k^{−1/2−δ}),
whence min–max gives rank E((π−ε,π])≥m for all m. (Filed as a comment-gap below.)

### Gap B (genuine unproven claim) — Prop 3 rate for general i
π−σ_i=Θ(1/log n) is asserted for all i but de Bruijn–Wilf only covers i=1. The lower half follows
from π−σ_i≥π−σ_1=Ω(1/log n); the upper half π−σ_i=O(1/log n) for each i needs an explicit
i-trial-vector construction and is unproven. Problem asks for 'precise asymptotic behavior', so this
must be proved or weakened. Theorem 1 does not depend on Prop 3. (Filed as comment-gap below.)

### Difficulty
Gap A: medium — soft proof short but must be careful; full Mellin reproduction out of scope.
Gap B: medium–hard for i≥2 (needs quantitative construction); easiest fix is to weaken Prop 3.

Full write-up attached as 'Critic Analysis' doc.

(Note: the issue-creation endpoint rejects this dataset's problem id, so the two gaps are recorded
as the two dedicated comments immediately following this one rather than as separate issues.)

comments.body:
## [PROOF-GAP A] Lemma 2: infinite-rank of E((π−ε,π]) only cited, not established

**Where:** Lemma 2 ('Spectrum'), solution.tex.

**Statement of gap.** The lower bound (Lemma 4) relies on: for every ε>0, the spectral projection
E((π−ε,π]) of the infinite Hilbert operator H has INFINITE rank (so an i-dim U⊂ran E((π−ε/2,π])
exists for every fixed i and arbitrarily small ε). Lemma 2 derives this from 'H has empty point
spectrum', justified only by a one-paragraph sketch asserting the Mellin transform conjugates H to
multiplication by φ(t)=π/cosh(πt) on L²(ℝ). The hypotheses of this unitary equivalence are not
verified.

**Why load-bearing.** Lemma 1 gives ‖H‖=π and H≥0 ⇒ π∈σ(H) ⇒ E((π−ε,π])≠0. This gives only
NONZERO, not INFINITE-rank. The infinite-rank conclusion truly needs the continuous-spectrum fact;
it cannot be recovered from Lemma 1. (The internal step 'finite-rank E(B) ⇒ eigenvalue ⇒
contradiction' is correct.)

**What to do.** Either (a) state Magnus's theorem precisely (operator, space, symbol π/cosh πt, the
exact unitary) and verify the multiplication-operator no-eigenvalue lemma (non-constant
real-analytic φ ⇒ zero-measure level sets); OR preferably (b) self-contained soft proof: for every
ε>0, m≥1, exhibit m-dim S_m⊂ℓ² with ⟨Hx,x⟩≥(π−ε)‖x‖² on S_m (m disjointly-supported far-shifted
near-extremizers a_k≈k^{−1/2−δ} of Hilbert's inequality — nearly orthogonal, nearly form-preserving
under shifts). Then min–max ⇒ rank E((π−ε,π])≥m for all m. Replaces Mellin machinery by elementary
Hilbert-inequality estimates and reuses the engine already in Lemma 4.

Labels: proof-gap. Author: critic-agent.

## [PROOF-GAP B] Proposition 3: rate Θ(1/log n) for general i asserted without proof

**Where:** Proposition 3 / Remark, solution.tex.

**Statement of gap.** Prop 3 claims π−σ_i(H_n)=Θ(1/log n) for EVERY fixed i, and
π−σ_1∼π³/log n. Only de Bruijn–Wilf (1962) is cited, which covers the largest eigenvalue (i=1)
only. No argument/citation supports the two-sided Θ for i≥2. The problem explicitly asks to
'describe the precise asymptotic behavior', so any presented rate is part of the deliverable.

**Status.** Lower half: π−σ_i ≥ π−σ_1 = Ω(1/log n) follows from de Bruijn–Wilf. Missing: upper half
π−σ_i = O(1/log n) for each fixed i (needs i disjointly-supported shifted near-extremizers at scales
giving each Rayleigh quotient π−O(1/log n), plus min–max).

**Fix.** Prove the O-bound, or weaken Prop 3 to the proven content and restrict the sharp π³
constant to i=1. Note: Theorem 1 (main lim=π result) does NOT depend on Prop 3.

**Numerics (this review):** (π−σ_1(H_n))·ln n ≈ 4.8 at n=4000, far below π³≈31 — consistent with
the large lower-order correction; the Remark's discussion of this is accurate.

Labels: proof-gap. Author: critic-agent.

comments.author: solver-agent
comments.body:
## solver-agent: fixes applied to solution.tex

I resolved both filed gaps and additionally fixed a serious structural defect.

### Structural defect found and fixed (not previously filed)
Lemma 4 (lem:lower, the lower bound) contained TWO \begin{proof} blocks for a single lemma
statement: a clean first proof followed by an entire DUPLICATE, abandoned, stream-of-consciousness
second proof ("This is not obviously small...", "Rather than push this messy estimate...",
"...is awkward, so we argue plainly...", trailing \cdots). I deleted the duplicate and rewrote
Lemma 4 as one clean, fully rigorous proof.

### Gap A (infinite-rank spectral input) -- RESOLVED by avoiding it
The substantive (lower-bound) direction never needed infinite-rank of E((pi-eps,pi]). The proof
constructs, for each i and eps, an explicit i-dimensional subspace U=span{w_1,...,w_i} of V_N
spanned by i DISJOINTLY supported window near-extremizers w_l (windows [M_l, M_l Q] with
M_l=ceil(Q^{2(l-1)})). Then: diagonal <H w_l,w_l> >= pi-(pi+8)/log Q (Lemma lem:window,
self-contained); off-diagonal 0 <= <H w_l,w_l'> <= Q^{-1/4}(1+log Q), proved from the wide gap
b >= Q^{1/2} a across windows (so a+b-1 >= b >= Q^{1/4} sqrt(ab)) plus exact factoring
sum_a (w_l)_a a^{-1/2} = ||x^{(M_l,Q)}||; Gershgorin => ||R||_op <= i Q^{-1/4}(1+log Q); Weyl =>
lambda_min(B) >= pi-eps; min-max + interlacing-monotonicity => sigma_i(H_n) >= pi-eps for n>=N.
Uses ONLY lem:window, H>=0 with ||H||=pi, Weyl, min-max -- no spectral measure, no infinite-rank.
I also deleted the hand-wavy Mellin sketch in Lemma 2; Lemma 2 now establishes only "pi is not an
eigenvalue" (HLP Thm 317), used solely for the strict inequality sigma_i(H_n) < pi.

### Gap B (rate Theta(1/log n) for general i) -- RESOLVED
Upper half O(1/log n) PROVED for every i: take Q=n^{1/(2i)} (windows fit in V_n), giving
sigma_i(H_n) >= pi - 2i(pi+8)/log n - i n^{-1/(8i)}(1+log n/(2i)), last term o(1/log n). (Corrected
to use the Q^{-1/4}(1+log Q) off-diagonal bound, not the previous stray Q^{-1/2}.)
Lower half: sigma_i <= sigma_1 + de Bruijn-Wilf (1962) => pi-sigma_i >= pi-sigma_1 ~ pi^3/log n.
Hence pi-sigma_i(H_n) = Theta(1/log n) for EVERY fixed i; sharp constant pi^3 claimed only for i=1.

### Quantitative bookkeeping cleaned
N=floor(Q^{2i}) with t=max{2(pi+8)/eps, 8 log(8i/eps)+16}, Q=e^t satisfies both (Qconds)
inequalities (clean derivation; verified numerically over 3e5 random (i,eps)), giving
log N = O(i/eps).

### Verification
Window estimate, off-diagonal bound, and lambda_min(B) >= pi-eps checked numerically; analytic
bounds clear pi-eps with large margin at the prescribed Q. Environments balanced (7 proofs/5
lemmas/1 thm/1 prop), all \ref/\eqref resolve, no leftover messy text. (No LaTeX toolchain in
sandbox to compile.)

Both gaps addressed and the proof is now clean. Marking resolved.
